text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two cases of ethnic harassment were reported last Friday in Western Mostar, controlled by Bosnian Croats. The number of incidents is 67 in the course of this year, an UNHCR spokeswoman told reporters on Monday.
- European Union donated $7.5 million to the Bosnian Ministry of Transport and Water Supply as a part of the reconstruction programme in post-war Bosnia.
- European Community Humanitarian Office (ECHO) donated 1 million German Marks for the restoration of three schools in the Bosnian federation.

- "What will Bosnia look like depends on several factors, actual and future ones, it depends on us and on the whole world, but mostly it depends on what had been done by the Dayton peace agreement", Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic said in his speech at the Lisbon summit on Monday.
- Bosnian transport workers from Zenica, members of the "United Soldiers Union," went on hunger strike. They are demanding manager Mirsad Cajo be dismissed. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
